## Which project

<!-- Project name and ID (near the top of its public page, like GF-2027-HI-082). -->

## Who is reporting

<!-- Your name and how to reach you. Kept for follow-up; never published. If you are reporting on someone else's behalf, name them as the source. -->

## The period

<!-- Which month, quarter, or season this covers (for example 2027-Q1, or Summer 2027). -->

## In the project's own words

<!-- One or two paragraphs, the way you would tell it to a neighbor. Say who is speaking. -->

## Results

<!-- One line per thing measured: what was measured — amount and unit — where the number comes from (crew log, count, lab report). Leave out what you do not have; blank is honest, zero is a claim. -->

## Place

<!-- The island and the moku the project serves, and the spot on the ground (a parcel number or a plain description). A project's results count in its moku, or not at all. -->

## Photo (optional)

<!-- Attach one you took or have permission to share. Say who took it and that the people in it agreed. -->

## Consent

- [ ] The project agrees these words and any photo may be published.

---

*What happens next:* this becomes a `draft` on the project's record. The
coordinator checks it within about a week and will ask in plain words if
anything is unclear. Once a reviewer approves, the project's page shows it.
Nothing publishes without those two people.
